title: Linear substitution identity for divided-power multinomial expressions
statement:
Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $f:A\to B$ a unital ring map, and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal with an ordinary divided-power structure $\gamma$ [def-sfb-ordinary-divided-power-structure]. For a finite tuple $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ in $I$, $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$ in $B$, and $n\geq0$, put
$$P_n(x;b)=\sum_{e\in\mathbb N^r,\;\sum_i e_i=n}\prod_{i=1}^r b_i^{e_i}f(\gamma_{e_i}(x_i)),$$
with $\gamma_0(x)=1$. For any $s\geq0$, $a_{ij}\in A$ and $c_j\in B$, put $b_i=\sum_{j=1}^s f(a_{ij})c_j$ and $y_j=\sum_{i=1}^r a_{ij}x_i$. Then $P_n(x;b)=P_n(y;c)$ for every $n\geq0$. Empty tuples, zero coefficients and zero ideals are allowed. No divided powers on any ideal of $B$ and no flatness of $f$ are assumed.

source.place: Tag 07H1 flat-case proof: matrix substitution identity preceding the common-refinement argument.

proof.text: Use finite coefficient arrays $u=(u_0,\ldots,u_n)$ over $B$, with $(u*v)_m=\sum_{p+q=m}u_pv_q$ for $0\le m\le n$, and unit $\delta_0=1$, $\delta_m=0$ for $m>0$. This is merely finite-sum notation. Commutativity swaps $(p,q)$; both $((u*v)*w)_m$ and $(u*(v*w))_m$ expand to $\sum_{p+q+t=m}u_pv_qw_t$, so convolution is associative. The unit assertion follows because only the term with zero index in $\delta$ survives. Thus finite convolution products may be reordered, including empty products $\delta$. Their $m$th entry is $\sum_{\sum_i e_i=m}\prod_i(u_i)_{e_i}$: for zero factors this is the convention for $\delta$; appending a factor gives exactly the displayed convolution sum.

source.place: Tag 07H1, lemma-gamma-extends, flat-case proof: displayed matrix-substitution identity; expansion using Tag 07GL, definition-divided-powers.

proof.text: For $z\in I$ and $t\in B$, write $E(z;t)_m=t^m f(\gamma_m(z))$ for $0\le m\le n$. From the scalar axiom with scalar zero, $\gamma_m(0)=0$ for $m>0$; $\gamma_0(0)=1$. Therefore $E(0;t)=\delta=E(z;0)$, using $0^0=1$. The degree-zero entries of all these arrays are $1$. In particular the coefficient-array convention deals with zero elements and with an empty tuple.

source.place: Tag 07H1, lemma-gamma-extends, flat-case proof: displayed matrix-substitution identity; expansion using Tag 07GL, definition-divided-powers.

proof.text:
For $z\in I$ and $t,u\in B$, the binomial theorem in the commutative ring $B$ gives
$$E(z;t+u)_m=\sum_{p+q=m}t^pu^q\binom mp f(\gamma_m(z))=\sum_{p+q=m}t^pu^q f(\gamma_p(z))f(\gamma_q(z)).$$
The second equality uses the product axiom $\gamma_p(z)\gamma_q(z)=\binom{p+q}{p}\gamma_{p+q}(z)$ when $p,q>0$; if one index is zero it follows from $\gamma_0(z)=1$ and the endpoint binomial coefficient $1$. For $m=0$ it is $1=1$. A unital ring map preserves these integer coefficients. Hence $E(z;t+u)=E(z;t)*E(z;u)$.

source.place: Tag 07H1, lemma-gamma-extends, flat-case proof: displayed matrix-substitution identity; expansion using Tag 07GL, definition-divided-powers.

proof.text:
For $z,w\in I$ and $t\in B$, the addition axiom and $t^{p+q}=t^pt^q$ give, entry by entry,
$$E(z+w;t)_m=\sum_{p+q=m}t^pt^q f(\gamma_p(z))f(\gamma_q(w))=(E(z;t)*E(w;t))_m.$$
This includes $m=0$, where both sides are $1$. For $a\in A$, the scalar axiom similarly gives $E(az;t)=E(z;f(a)t)$, including degree zero. All ideal-membership hypotheses hold since $I$ is an ideal.

source.place: Tag 07H1, lemma-gamma-extends, flat-case proof: displayed matrix-substitution identity; expansion using Tag 07GL, definition-divided-powers.

proof.text:
Repeated use of step 3 yields $E(z;\sum_j t_j)=\mathop{*}_j E(z;t_j)$: the empty case is step 2 and the successor case splits off the last summand by step 3. In the same way step 4 and $E(0;t)=\delta$ give $E(\sum_i z_i;t)=\mathop{*}_i E(z_i;t)$ for every finite tuple in $I$. Apply these identities with $t_j=f(a_{ij})c_j$ and $z_i=a_{ij}x_i$; every $z_i$ lies in $I$ and every $t_j$ lies in $B$. The scalar identity of step 4 then gives
$$\mathop{*}_i E(x_i;b_i)=\mathop{*}_i\mathop{*}_j E(a_{ij}x_i;c_j)=\mathop{*}_j\mathop{*}_i E(a_{ij}x_i;c_j)=\mathop{*}_j E(y_j;c_j).$$
The middle equality reorders the same finite list of $rs$ factors using step 1. Taking the $n$th entry and the finite-product formula of step 1 is exactly $P_n(x;b)=P_n(y;c)$. If either index set is empty, both corresponding products are $\delta$, so the argument also covers $r=0$ or $s=0$.

lean.statement: theorem dpow_multinomial_linear_substitution {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) (I : Ideal A) (γ : DividedPowers I) (r s : ℕ) (x : Fin r → A) (hx : ∀ i : Fin r, x i ∈ I) (a : Fin r → Fin s → A) (c : Fin s → B) (n : ℕ) : (∑ e ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin r)).sym n, ∏ i : Fin r, (∑ j : Fin s, f (a i j) * c j) ^ Multiset.count i e * f (γ.dpow (Multiset.count i e) (x i))) = ∑ d ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin s)).sym n, ∏ j : Fin s, c j ^ Multiset.count j d * f (γ.dpow (Multiset.count j d) (∑ i : Fin r, a i j * x i))
